samples.summary: Deck-non-empty invariant is enforced only in the UI, not in the store (`removeSlides` is an unguarded filter)
samples.evidence: The new heal's own comment (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:1546-1550) documents that `removeSlides` accepts any id set and that the only "don't delete the last slide" gate lives in the thumbnail panel (packages/slides/src/view/editor/thumbnail-panel.ts:320). `MemSlidesStore.removeSlides` (memory.ts:271-275) is a bare `filter` with no non-empty check, and `LayoutEditStore.removeSlides` (layout-edit-store.ts:175) is a no-op, so the model layer has no invariant. Vector, such as it is: a collaborator (or a crafted CRDT op from a peer that skips the local UI path) empties the deck, and every client is driven into the empty-deck branch (`currentId = undefined`, teardown of edit/crop) purely from remote input. Note this is validation-in-the-UI-only, not an authorization boundary — a peer that can send ops already holds write access to the document — so the impact is availability/data-integrity hardening rather than privilege escalation. I could not find any server-side or store-side structural validation of incoming slide mutations. This change makes the client survive that state rather than blanking, so it is an improvement; the finding is that the invariant still has no enforced home.
searchedFor: Grep readonly|readOnly|canEdit|permission across packages/slides/src (no editor-level permission gate exists)
